title: R
label: R
desc: Statistical language built around vectors, data frames, and the tidyverse.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Check the interpreter, install the packages used below, and run a script

snippets.code:
# Version of the interpreter on the PATH
R --version

# Install packages from CRAN once per R version
Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("tidyverse", "readxl"), repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")'

# Run a script non-interactively
Rscript analysis.R

# Open the interactive REPL
R

# Load the tidyverse: dplyr, tidyr, ggplot2, readr, purrr
library(tidyverse)

# R version, platform, and every attached package
sessionInfo()

# Working directory and R version as a string
getwd()
R.version.string

sections.title: Syntax
sections.description: Arrow assignment, vectors as the base type, string building, and namespaces

snippets.code:
# Assignment uses the arrow, = only binds function arguments
x <- 42
name <- "Ada"
ratio <- 0.75
flag <- TRUE

# Everything is a vector, even a single value
length(x)    # 1
class(ratio) # "numeric"

# Strings: paste0 joins without a separator, sprintf formats
paste0("id-", x)                       # "id-42"
sprintf("%s scored %.1f", name, ratio) # "Ada scored 0.8"

# Comments run to the end of the line

# Indexing starts at 1, negative indices drop elements
values <- c(10, 20, 30, 40)
values[1]       # 10
values[-2]      # 10 30 40
values[c(2, 4)] # 20 40

# A double colon reaches an export without attaching the package
mtcars |> dplyr::filter(cyl == 4) |> nrow() # 11

sections.title: Vectors
sections.description: c(), sequences, recycling, names, and logical indexing

snippets.code:
# c() builds a vector, all elements share one type
numbers <- c(4, 8, 15, 16, 23, 42)
mixed <- c(1, "two", TRUE) # coerced to character
mixed
# [1] "1"   "two" "TRUE"

# Sequences and repeats
seq(0, 1, by = 0.25)        # 0.00 0.25 0.50 0.75 1.00
rep(c("a", "b"), times = 3) # "a" "b" "a" "b" "a" "b"

# Arithmetic recycles the shorter vector
c(1, 2, 3) * 2 # 2 4 6

scores <- c(ana = 91, bruno = 78, carla = 85)

# Names travel with the vector
names(scores)   # "ana" "bruno" "carla"
scores["carla"] # carla 85

# Logical indexing keeps the matching positions
scores[scores >= 85]
scores[names(scores) == "bruno"]

# Summary helpers ignore names, na.rm drops missing values
mean(scores)      # 84.66667
max(scores)       # 91
sum(is.na(scores)) # 0

sections.title: Data Frames
sections.description: Column access, row filters, and the bracket versus dollar distinction

snippets.code:
# A data frame is a list of equal-length vectors
orders <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  customer = c("ana", "bruno", "carla", "diego"),
  total = c(120.5, 80, 240.9, 15),
  paid = c(TRUE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
)

str(orders)
nrow(orders) # 4
ncol(orders) # 4

# $ pulls a vector, ["col"] keeps a one-column data frame
orders$total
orders[, "total"]
orders["total"]

# Row filter and column selection in one bracket call
unpaid <- orders[!orders$paid, c("id", "customer")]
unpaid
#   id customer
# 3  3    carla

# Add a computed column
orders$total_with_fee <- orders$total * 1.1
head(orders, 2)

# order() returns the permutation that sorts the rows
orders[order(-orders$total), ]

sections.title: Lists
sections.description: Heterogeneous containers, single versus double brackets, and nested access

snippets.code:
# A list holds anything, including other lists
report <- list(
  title = "March revenue",
  total = 41250.75,
  months = c("jan", "feb", "mar"),
  owner = list(name = "ana", team = "finance")
)

report$total        # 41250.75
report[["months"]]  # "jan" "feb" "mar"
report$owner$name   # "ana"
length(report)      # 4

# Single brackets keep a sub-list, double brackets extract the element
report["total"]          # list(total = 41250.75)
report[["total"]]        # 41250.75
class(report["total"])   # "list"
class(report[["total"]]) # "numeric"

# Add and remove entries
report$quarter <- "Q1"
report$owner <- NULL
names(report) # "title" "total" "months" "quarter"

sections.title: Factors
sections.description: Categorical data with fixed levels, ordering, and counts per level

snippets.code:
# Factors store categories with a fixed set of levels
sizes <- factor(c("M", "S", "L", "M", "XL"), levels = c("S", "M", "L", "XL"))
sizes
# [1] M  S  L  M  XL
# Levels: S M L XL

levels(sizes)     # "S" "M" "L" "XL"
as.integer(sizes) # 2 1 3 2 4, the level codes
table(sizes)      # counts per level

# Ordered factors compare with < and >
rating <- factor(c("low", "high", "medium", "high"),
                 levels = c("low", "medium", "high"), ordered = TRUE)
rating[1] < rating[2] # TRUE

# relevel moves a reference level, useful before modelling
levels(relevel(sizes, ref = "M")) # "M" "S" "L" "XL"

# Drop levels that no row uses any more
droplevels(factor(c("S", "S"), levels = c("S", "M", "L")))

sections.title: Functions
sections.description: Default arguments, early returns, functions as values, and error handling

snippets.code:
# Functions are values, so they can be passed and stored
apply_twice <- function(f, x) f(f(x))
apply_twice(sqrt, 256) # 4

# stopifnot fails fast on bad input
ratio <- function(part, whole) {
  stopifnot(whole > 0, part >= 0)
  part / whole
}
ratio(3, 4) # 0.75

# tryCatch turns an error into a value
tryCatch(ratio(1, 0), error = function(e) NA_real_) # NA

sections.title: The apply Family
sections.description: apply over margins, lapply and sapply over lists, mapply and tapply over groups

snippets.code:
m <- matrix(1:6, nrow = 2)
m
#      [,1] [,2] [,3]
# [1,]    1    3    5
# [2,]    2    4    6

apply(m, 1, sum)  # 9 12, by row
apply(m, 2, mean) # 1.5 3.5 5.5, by column

values <- list(a = 1:3, b = 4:6, c = 7:9)

# lapply always returns a list, sapply simplifies when it can
lapply(values, mean) # $a 2, $b 5, $c 8
sapply(values, mean) # a b c / 2 5 8

# vapply states the return type, so a surprise fails loudly
vapply(values, mean, numeric(1))

# mapply walks several vectors in parallel
mapply(function(x, y) x^y, c(2, 3), c(3, 2)) # 8 9

# tapply splits one vector by a grouping vector
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$cyl, mean)
#        4        6        8
# 26.66364 19.74286 15.10000

sections.title: dplyr
sections.description: filter, select, mutate, grouped summaries with .by, joins, and across

snippets.code:
library(dplyr)

sales <- tibble::tibble(
  region = c("sul", "sul", "norte", "norte", "sul"),
  month = c("jan", "feb", "jan", "feb", "mar"),
  revenue = c(1200, 1500, 900, 1100, 1800),
  orders = c(40, 52, 30, 35, 61)
)

sales |>
  filter(revenue > 1000) |>
  select(region, month, revenue) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue))

# mutate adds columns, summarise collapses rows
sales |>
  mutate(ticket = revenue / orders) |>
  summarise(
    revenue = sum(revenue),
    ticket = mean(ticket),
    .by = region
  )

targets <- tibble::tibble(region = c("norte", "sul"), goal = c(2500, 5000))

# Joins keep the left rows and add the matching columns
sales |>
  summarise(revenue = sum(revenue), .by = region) |>
  left_join(targets, by = "region") |>
  mutate(gap = goal - revenue, hit = revenue >= goal)

# across applies one function to several columns
sales |>
  summarise(across(c(revenue, orders), mean, .names = "{.col}_avg"), .by = region)

sections.title: tidyr and Pipes
sections.description: Reshape wide and long data, split columns, and chain steps with the native pipe

snippets.code:
wide <- tibble::tibble(
  store = c("centro", "shopping"),
  q1 = c(120, 90),
  q2 = c(150, 110)
)

# Wide to long: one row per store and quarter
wide |>
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("q"), names_to = "quarter", values_to = "revenue")
# store    quarter revenue
# centro   q1        120
# centro   q2        150
# shopping q1         90

long <- tibble::tibble(
  store = c("centro", "centro", "shopping"),
  quarter = c("q1", "q2", "q1"),
  revenue = c(120, 150, 90)
)

# Long to wide, filling gaps with a real value
long |> pivot_wider(names_from = quarter, values_from = revenue, values_fill = 0)

# Native pipe, R 4.1 and later
long |> dplyr::filter(revenue > 100) |> nrow() # 2

# Split one character column into several
codes <- tibble::tibble(code = c("sul-01", "norte-07"))
codes |> separate_wider_delim(code, delim = "-", names = c("region", "id"))

sections.title: ggplot2
sections.description: Build a plot in layers, map aesthetics, facet, and save at a fixed size

snippets.code:
library(ggplot2)

monthly <- tibble::tibble(
  month = factor(c("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr"), levels = c("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr")),
  revenue = c(1200, 1500, 1800, 1400),
  channel = c("loja", "loja", "online", "online")
)

ggplot(monthly, aes(x = month, y = revenue)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#276DC3") +
  labs(title = "Revenue by month", x = NULL, y = "BRL") +
  theme_minimal()

# Layers stack with +, each geom inherits the mapping from ggplot()
ggplot(monthly, aes(x = month, y = revenue, group = channel, color = channel)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(big.mark = ".")) +
  facet_wrap(~channel) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# ggsave uses the device implied by the extension
ggsave("revenue.png", width = 7, height = 4, dpi = 150)

sections.title: Reading and Writing
sections.description: CSV with base R and readr, Excel sheets, JSON, and R's own binary format

snippets.code:
# Base R needs no package
orders <- read.csv("data/orders.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA"))
str(orders)

# readr is faster, guesses types, and never makes factors on its own
library(readr)
orders <- read_csv("data/orders.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

write_csv(orders, "data/orders_clean.csv")

# RDS keeps types and factors exactly, no parsing on the way back
saveRDS(orders, "data/orders.rds")
orders <- readRDS("data/orders.rds")

# Excel: first sheet by default, skip rows above the header
readxl::read_excel("data/report.xlsx", sheet = "March", skip = 2)

# JSON becomes a nested list, simplifyVector makes data frames where it can
jsonlite::fromJSON("data/orders.json", simplifyVector = TRUE)

sections.title: Statistics
sections.description: Descriptives, grouped means, linear models, and the common hypothesis tests

snippets.code:
# Descriptives
mean(mtcars$mpg)   # 20.09062
median(mtcars$mpg) # 19.2
sd(mtcars$mpg)     # 6.026948
quantile(mtcars$mpg, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))

# Grouped means without extra packages
aggregate(mpg ~ cyl, data = mtcars, FUN = mean)

# Linear model: mpg explained by weight and cylinder count
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt + factor(cyl), data = mtcars)
summary(fit)
confint(fit)

# Predictions for new rows
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(wt = c(2.5, 3.5), cyl = c(4, 6)))

# Tests
t.test(mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 1], mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 0])
cor.test(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg, method = "pearson") # r = -0.8676594
chisq.test(table(mtcars$cyl, mtcars$gear))

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: The messages that stop a session, and the one-line fix for each

snippets.code:
# object not found: the name was never assigned here
mean(revenue)
# Error in mean(revenue): object 'revenue' not found
mean(sales$revenue) # refer to the column explicitly

# $ is invalid on an atomic vector
numbers <- c(10, 20, 30)
numbers$value
# Error: $ operator is invalid for atomic vectors
numbers[1] # use indexing instead

# if() needs one TRUE or FALSE, NA stops it
x <- NA
if (x > 0) print("positive")
# Error in if (x > 0) print("positive"): missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
if (isTRUE(x > 0)) print("positive") else print("not positive")

# Numbers that arrived as text
df <- data.frame(amount = c("10", "20"))
mean(df$amount)
# Error in mean.default(df$amount): argument is not numeric or logical
mean(as.numeric(df$amount)) # 15

# Replacement length must match the row count
df$flag <- c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE)
# Error: replacement has 3 rows, data has 2
